title: Finite locally free strict transform after an admissible blow-up
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $X\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $U\subseteq S$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume that the restriction $X\times_S U\to U$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then there exist a $U$-admissible blow-up $b:S'\to S$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] and a finite locally free morphism from the strict transform $X'\to S'$ [def-nagata-strict-transform, def-pc-finite-locally-free].

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-nagata-boundary-divisor] to $S$ and $U$, obtaining a $U$-admissible blow-up $b_0:S_0\to S$ for which $U_0=b_0^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense. The map $b_0$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], hence quasi-compact and separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] it is quasi-separated, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) makes $S_0$ qcqs. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], $U_0\to U$ is an isomorphism; in particular $U_0$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0B49 proof, schematic-density reduction; flat.tex remark-successive-blowups; Divisors Tags 02OS and 07ZU.

proof.text: For the blow-ups in this proof the strict transform is a closed subscheme of the ambient base change by [def-nagata-strict-transform], read in its current scheme-image formulation. Its restriction over the preserved open is the original restriction: [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] identifies the base over that open with the original base, and [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] restricts the closure-defining scheme image there. The open immersion defining this image is quasi-compact: locally in an affine of the ambient scheme, the pulled-back finite-type center ideal has finitely many generators, so its complement is a finite union of principal affine opens. It is quasi-separated since it is an open immersion. After restriction, this open immersion is the identity on the whole ambient restriction, whose scheme image is itself (its restriction kernel is zero). This proves the asserted identification with the original restriction, including its scheme structure.

source.place: Divisors Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; Morphisms Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, restriction to an open. The restriction kernel on the identity open is zero.

proof.text: Let $f_0:X_0\to S_0$ be the strict transform along $b_0$. Its closed inclusion into $X\times_S S_0$, followed by the base change of the given proper $X\to S$, is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a)--(c). Thus $f_0$ is of finite type and separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Step 2 identifies $(X_0)_{U_0}\to U_0$ with the original $X_U\to U$, so it is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Apply [lem-trf-flattening-by-admissible-blowup] to $(S_0,U_0,f_0)$. All its hypotheses have now been checked. It gives a $U_0$-admissible blow-up $b_1:S_1\to S_0$ and a strict transform $f_1:X_1\to S_1$ which is flat and of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 0B49 and 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up; properness permanence: Morphisms Tags 01W3, 01W4 and 01W5.

proof.text: The closed inclusion $X_1\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{S_0}S_1$ and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a)--(c) show that $f_1$ is still proper. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density], applied to the quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open $U_0\subseteq S_0$ and the finite-type center of $b_1$, the open $U_1=b_1^{-1}(U_0)$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $S_1$. It is topologically dense as well: if a nonempty affine open $V\subseteq S_1$ missed $U_1$, the injection $\mathcal O_{S_1}\to (j_1)_*\mathcal O_{U_1}$ of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open] would inject the nonzero ring $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)$ into zero, a contradiction. Step 2 identifies $(X_1)_{U_1}\to U_1$ with $X_U\to U$, which is finite. The finite-presentation conclusion of Step 3 includes local finite presentation. Therefore [lem-trf-proper-flat-finite-dense-open] applies to $f_1$ and $U_1$, proving that $f_1$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0B49 proof, application of Tag 0B48, lemma-proper-flat-finite-over-dense-open; schematic-density preparation in remark-successive-blowups and the cited blueprint lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density.

proof.text: The morphism $f_1$ is finite by Step 4, and flat and locally of finite presentation by Step 3. It is therefore finite locally free by exactly the definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 0B49 last sentence, Morphisms Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat; the project definition already uses its finite, flat and locally-of-finite-presentation characterization.

proof.text: Write $b_0=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ and $b_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(S_0)\to S_0$ using their admissible center data. The current statement of [thm-nagata-composition-of-blowups] supplies a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ on $S$ and an isomorphism $S_1\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(S)$ over $S$, with $V(\mathcal K)=V(\mathcal I)\cup b_0(V(\mathcal J))$. Both terms are disjoint from $U$: the first by admissibility of $b_0$, the second because $V(\mathcal J)$ misses $U_0=b_0^{-1}(U)$. Thus $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and this presentation makes $b=b_0b_1$ a single $U$-admissible blow-up by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-composition] with these three ideals and this specified isomorphism. Its support-equality hypothesis is exactly the equality supplied above, and it identifies $X_1$ with the strict transform of the original $X$ along $b$. Consequently that strict transform is finite locally free by Step 5, as required.
